name: Halloween Gambit
summary: The Halloween Gambit (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nxe5 Nxe5 5.d4) sacrifices a knight for a broad pawn centre and attacking chances.
intro: The Halloween Gambit is a shock weapon in the Four Knights Game, arising after 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Nxe5, when White simply captures a central pawn with the knight and offers the piece. Following 4...Nxe5 5.d4, the pawn drives the knight backward and White erects an imposing pawn duo on e4 and d4, hoping to sweep the black pieces off their natural squares. Objectively the gambit is unsound, since accurate defence lets Black consolidate the extra material, yet its startling nature makes it a genuine practical try. It is best known from correspondence and online blitz play, where the surprise value and gain of time can quickly overwhelm an unprepared opponent.
line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe5 d4

sections.heading: Strategic ideas
paragraphs: White's whole concept is to trade a knight for a dominating pawn centre and a lead in development. After 5.d4 the e5-knight must retreat, and White follows with e4-e5 to chase the f6-knight as well, gaining tempi while cramping Black's kingside. If the black pieces are pushed to awkward squares, White's rapid deployment of bishops and queen can generate a swift attack against f7 and the uncastled king.

For Black the guiding principle is to keep calm, give back a portion of the material at the right moment, and complete development. Returning the extra piece with ideas like ...Ng6 followed by ...d6, or an early ...Bb4 and ...d6, blunts the pawn centre and leaves Black with a healthy, often superior position. Because the gambit relies on the initiative rather than on any lasting compensation, once Black neutralizes the attack the extra pawn or piece simply tells.

sections.heading: Main variations
paragraphs: After 5.d4 the knight most commonly retreats to g6, when 6.e5 attacks the f6-knight and 6...Ng8 or 6...Ng4 leads to sharp play, though the fashionable defensive setup runs 6...Ng4 or the solid 5...Ng6 6.e5 Ng8 with ...d6 to come. A frequently recommended antidote is to meet the pawn storm with ...Bb4 pinning the c3-knight and ...d6 undermining the e5-pawn, after which Black returns material and unravels comfortably.

White's attacking tries typically involve Bc4 targeting f7, f2-f4-f5 to expand, and quick castling, but precise defence repeatedly demonstrates that the two pawns and initiative do not fully compensate for the sacrificed knight. Because the position after 5.d4 is so committal, small inaccuracies by either side can swing the evaluation dramatically, which is exactly what makes the line so effective as a surprise in fast games.

sections.heading: History and background
paragraphs: The Halloween Gambit belongs to the family of romantic-era piece sacrifices in the open games, and its various names reflect a murky history of independent rediscovery. It was analyzed by nineteenth-century players and later championed in correspondence circles, gaining fresh notoriety in the early internet era as a favourite of engine-assisted analysts and blitz specialists. The colourful name evokes the fright the sacrifice is meant to give an unsuspecting opponent. While top-level theory regards it as dubious against best play, it endures as an instructive example of the value of a mobile pawn centre and rapid development.

keyIdeas: In the Four Knights, White plays the shock sacrifice 4.Nxe5 Nxe5 5.d4.
The point is to gain a big e4/d4 pawn centre for the sacrificed knight.
White follows with e4-e5 to chase pieces and gain attacking tempi.
Black defends best by returning material with ...Ng6/...d6 or ...Bb4.
Objectively unsound, but a dangerous surprise in blitz and correspondence play.
The compensation is initiative, not permanent structural gain.

white: Build the broad centre with d4 and advance e4-e5 to harass the knights.
Develop quickly with Bc4 to pressure the sensitive f7-square.
Castle and open lines toward Black's uncastled king before he consolidates.
Use f2-f4-f5 to expand the pawn front and create attacking threats.
Keep the initiative flowing, since the gambit offers no long-term compensation.
black: Stay calm and aim to return part of the material to defuse the attack.
Retreat the knight to g6 and prepare ...d6 to challenge the e5-pawn.
Pin the c3-knight with ...Bb4 to slow White's central expansion.
Complete development and castle into safety before pressing the extra material.
Convert the material edge once White's initiative has been neutralized.
